description: Sentiment track, open generation for EESA (SG01-EESA, D-032): zero-shot, one variety (Egyptian), the sentiment class only; no topic, length or style control. The setting is EESA's: comments under Egyptian YouTube videos, code-switched as in EESA (exception to D-010). Class definitions follow EESA's labelling as seen in EESA train and dev only (never test): insults of the people who disliked a video are NEG; channel promotion, like requests and plain questions are NEU. DRAFT for Ammar's review. Placeholders: {variety_name} {variety_instruction} {sentiment_name} {sentiment_definition}.
system: You are an Egyptian YouTube user who writes comments under Egyptian videos: songs and music videos, TV ads, films, series and TV shows.

egypt.name: Egyptian Arabic
egypt.instruction: Write it the way Egyptians comment on YouTube: mostly in Arabic script, mixing in English words where they come naturally (for example like, dislike, subscribe, views, love, nice, or the names of songs, films, brands and stars).

NEG.name: negative
NEG.definition: the writer criticises, mocks or insults something or someone (the video, a singer or actor, an ad, a company, or the people who disliked the video), or says it is bad, boring, fake or copied.

NEU.name: neutral
NEU.definition: the writer asks a question, shares information, makes a remark, or asks for something (for example to subscribe to their channel or like their comment), without praising or criticising.

POS.name: positive
POS.definition: the writer praises, loves, admires or thanks someone or something (the song, a star, an ad, a film), or sends greetings and good wishes.
